prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System advises; command retains authority; no autonomous dispatch/control. Aliases: Duty Detection Officer=Orion; Air Attack Supervisor=Redtail; Caldera Incident Command Portal=Emberhall; Horizon Ridge Drone Dock=Kestrel; Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine=Lantern; MesoWest Weather Fusion Node=Brindle; Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console=Marigold; VHF Radio Gateway Repeater=Badger. Orion accepts Smoke Classifier Module likelihood/growth/obscuration/confidence/Ridge Shadow Mask; degraded classifier is down-weighted, never sole aircraft-commitment basis. North Lookout Camera Mast sends Thermal Spot Snippet/bearings; South Lookout Camera Mast sends triangulation bearings/Camera Cleaning Log. Brindle quality-checks/interpolates weather, publishes Wind Shift Bulletin/time-indexed recomputations. Lantern compares reconnaissance/cameras/weather; models accepted perimeter/growth/weather/fuels into probability bands. Conflicts require review before promotion; Delayed Confirmed Ignition State blocks premature dispatch. Redtail reviews promoted location/confidence history/airspace before reconnaissance/retardant authorization; bulletin informs sequencing/holding/drop direction. Airspace Restricted State limits dispatch until Redtail accepts route/altitude. Drone Tasking Service packages approved missions with launch windows/image requirements/altitude limits/abort criteria; avoids aviation lanes, cannot release. Kestrel charges/positions/launches/recovers/shelters aircraft; must report readiness/health/recovery availability before release. Maintenance controller produces Battery Swap Ticket. Drone Pilot Operator verifies field-route safety/noninterference. County Emergency Liaison sends Drone Corridor Permit. Imagery requires orthorectification/grid-registration; verifies access/spread/structure exposure before crew commitment. Marigold tracks availability/arrival/turnaround/priority; blocks release without approvals/airspace/readiness; produces Runway Release Note after runway-sequence validation. East Retardant Loading Pump produces Retardant Batch Slip; Tanker Base Manager verifies assignment/quantity, coordinates West Retardant Loading Pump, resolves discrepancies. Both pumps report state/flow/outages; loading status is not approval. Badger relays approved instructions during connectivity degradation. Emberhall provides role-based overlays/Crew Staging Pin(time/accuracy/incident-ID), retains provenance/confidence/sensor-age/position-error/decisions, not assignments/notifications. Crewline Mobile Tablet delivers released context; Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges/reports occupancy; supervisor

New part:
S146: The Crewline Mobile Tablet shows approved suppression objectives, aircraft caution areas, and current assignment notes for crews operating near the incident.
S147: The Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges nearby aircraft activity before personnel are moved into a drop zone or a reconnaissance overflight area.
S148: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console sends the Suppression Drop Receipt after a completed drop has been recorded and checked for required timing fields.
S149: During extended attack, the Caldera Incident Command Portal preserves each aviation decision with the approving supervisor, operational period, and reason for change.
S150: The County Emergency Liaison can view approved aviation status and public safety implications without gaining authority to alter dispatch or suppression records.
S151: If reconnaissance, loading status, or weather guidance conflicts with an active plan, the system holds the affected recommendation for Air Attack Supervisor review before further action.
S152: This section describes how helitack and ground crews receive assignments, staging information, hazards, and updated intelligence from the support system during active wildfire operations.
S153: When a held recommendation is cleared, the Air Attack Supervisor selects the operational intent in the Caldera Incident Command Portal.
S154: The Caldera Incident Command Portal records each assignment package with an objective, time validity, confirmation status, and required acknowledgments.
S155: The Crewline Mobile Tablet displays the current division assignment, route guidance, rally location, and assigned communications channel for the logged-in crew.
S156: The Helitack Crew Leader receives the same operational package with aviation constraints and landing zone notes after Air Attack Supervisor approval.
S157: Ground crew assignments are formatted for field execution and avoid analytic scores that are not needed for tactical movement.
S158: Staging information is maintained as georeferenced areas and route descriptions so that crews can confirm location without relying on informal landmarks.
S159: The Crewline Mobile Tablet caches the latest accepted staging information and marks any expired package as unavailable for execution.
S160: If the Confirmed Ignition State changes the perimeter or priority area, the Caldera Incident Command Portal marks affected crew assignments for review before release.
S161: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine updates hazard summaries when fire spread estimates, access constraints, or field observations change.
S162: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine applies the Ridge Shadow Mask when estimating crew-visible fire edge confidence in steep terrain.
S163: The Smoke Classifier Module uses the Camera Cleaning Log to suppress confidence changes caused by lens contamination and service timing.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
